observation.visible_scene: A rocky mountain stream captured from a low, fixed viewpoint. Large lichen-flecked granite boulders occupy the left and bottom foreground; a thin bare twig protrudes from the water near the center; a cluster of rounded rocks lines the right bank; and a small white waterfall pours in the upper-left background. A pool of aerated, churning white water fills the mid- and foreground.
visible_changes: The foreground water surface continuously churns: foam, bubbles, and ripples form, shift downstream, and dissipate from frame to frame.
The central bare twig flexes and sways slightly, its tip bending and repositioning as the turbulent flow passes around it.
The background waterfall's white plume stays broadly steady in shape and position.
The foreground boulders, right-bank rocks, and background elements hold identical positions across all frames, indicating no camera movement.
Lighting and color tone remain constant throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The segment is a temporal crop; the water flow was already underway at t=0 and continues past t=2.667, so no start or stop of motion is shown.
The cause of the waterfall, the stream's full extent, and any scenery beyond the frame edges are unseen.
uncertain_details: Whether the twig's apparent motion is true elastic flexing or partly occlusion by passing foam cannot be confirmed.
The precise net direction of the foreground current is ambiguous amid the turbulence.
No object enters or leaves the frame; all changes are confined to the moving water and the swaying twig.
